name: general-library

building.also_note: no other building of the campus map: measured 2026-10-22 from the round-0 model's footprint (cells above 2.5 m, 0.5 m grid, run.sh topview) it covers 94.1% of 109's block and under 0.5% of any other block within 80 m.
building.title: General Library, University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 109's outline from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; used only to choose the crop box, to pick the building's own points (frame.near_outline) and to draw on the heightmap figure; the frame comes from the LiDAR.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: view frame: the foot of the main entrance in the south-east end, toward its back corner (bsR6's wide view, 2025-05: the doors under the name board, about 7 m behind the slab's back face line seen from the street side); the LiDAR ground on the footway there is 41.45-41.55 m, so ground is 41.5 and the model's y is 0 there; place.py puts it on the map

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) within near_outline m of building 109's outline: centre = mean x/y of points higher than tower_above m: the roof of the tower slab and the plant room on it; axis = the bearing of most of the walls seen from above (axis_from walls), the one of the two square to each other nearest the principal axis of the points from min_above to spine_below m within spine_radius m of the centre, pointing north-ish as street_side is west; toStreet = the axis turned 90 deg toward street_side: south-west, to Alfred Street.

streetview.pano_ids_note: the twelve Google panoramas pinned on 2026-10-22, each showing the building: six on Alfred Street in front of the south-west face (2022-09: B4NW, MMME, w8_f, CHbl, v7l7, vbVX, 25-37 m from the slab's centre), three at the south-east end and its corner (2025-05: bsR6, 3HyL, xKYw), two behind on the north-east (2025-05: Zvdo, fF8q) and one on Princes Street off the north-west end (2024-07: Qaci). Of the 63 panoramas within 120 m, 50 are Google's and 13 user-contributed (left out). The 26 Google panoramas within 75 m were looked at in a low-resolution probe (zoom 3, 148 tiles, 126 of them bought): 22 show the building; of the others, vbf9 and ln-V see trees, BzLX a bus and nAxE trees and Old Choral Hall. Left out though they show it: Ac3I (beside bsR6, the same view), -JHj and uM18 (close to the back's lower walls), dyTf and u2Aj (Alfred Street further west, through trees), FgM3 and e8T_ (further east), EX9b (behind, beside fF8q), S1Vu and B-1T (Princes Street, beside Qaci). 1,650 zoom-5 tiles were bought for the twelve: 1,776 for this building with the probe.

light.note: the viewer's light for this building (pipeline/viewer/main.js; the address still wins): the twelve panoramas are of spring (2022-09) and autumn (2025-05) days, the street faces mostly in soft light; exposure 0.8 brings the white concrete nearer the photographs' (round 0: building region luma p50, photographs 142, render 178 at 1.0)

ground_note: provisional: the LiDAR ground on the footway at the main entrance, in the middle of the south-east end (41.45 to 41.55 m at x 30.5 to 32, z -8; the site falls about 5 m from Princes Street on the west, 45.6 m, to 40.6 m at the north-east corner, and Alfred Street in front of the south-west face is 43.3 to 44.8 m); the frame's thresholds are above this ground (2.5 m more than with the first, provisional 44.0, so the frame is the same); set at the door once the references show it
